articles.title: The Prem: Saracens 17-21 Sale: Sharks beat Sarries despite red card
articles.summary: Sale overcome Jacques Vermeulen's red card to defeat Saracens 21-17 and pick up their first win of The Prem campaign.
articles.body:
Tries: Mawi, Va'enuku, C Bracken Cons: Burke

Tries: Jibulu, O'Flaherty, Bamber Cons: Ford 2, Lozowski

Sale overcame Jacques Vermeulen's red card to defeat Saracens and pick up their first win of The Prem campaign.

Sarries struggled to break down a stubborn Sharks defence despite having numerical superiority for 27 minutes of the first half after Alex Lozowski's yellow and Vermeulen's 20-minute red card.

Incredibly, Sale took a 7-5 lead into half-time thanks to Nathan Jibulu's early converted try, despite Eroni Mawi's reply, and then went further ahead soon after the break as Tom O'Flaherty raced in.

Ben Bamber stretched Sale's lead to 11 points after Sione Va'enuku had cut the gap, and though Charlie Bracken's late score again put the game in the balance, the hosts held on.

After shipping 150 points to Saracens in two Prem hammerings last season, Sale's victory at the Stone X was built on a huge defensive effort.

Their forwards laid down an impressive early marker when a driving maul carved through Sarries with relative ease to sweep Jibulu over the line.

But the visitors were soon down to 13 as former Sarrie Alex Lozowski was yellow-carded for a high shot on Barbeary on his first Sale start before Vermeulen was red-carded for putting a shoulder into Tomos Williams' head.

And only a TMO intervention prevented the visitors going down to 12 when Hamish Smales overturned Courtney Lawes' yellow card for a deliberate knock on.

Smales was involved again to overturn Nick Tompkins' smart close-range finish for a Nick Isiekwe's obstruction in the build-up, but Mawi finally turned Sarries' red-zone pressure into points when he powered over.

Yet Sale were heartened to head into half-time with a two-point lead and back up to full strength as Elia Canakaivata replaced Vermeulen.

Saracens responded with three changes at half-time, including a debut for England lock George Martin, but Sale soon went nine points clear when O'Flaherty collected George Ford's up and under on halfway and raced away to score.

The hosts finally found their cutting edge when a quick switch of play while camped on the Sale line created an overlap and gave Va'Enuku a walk-in on debut.

Sale's defence continued to impress before a quick change of pace in attack sent them 21-10 up as Ford teed up Bamber to run a hard line through a gap and race in.

Once again the Sarries response was swift as Jack Bracken cut in off the right wing to give brother Charlie a clear run to the line to set up a tense finale.

Venter explains wine reference as job title confirmed

Despite opening the season with an eventful and impressive 40-38 win over Leicester , Brendan Venter made most of the headlines in its aftermath.

The former South Africa international was reported to have changed his job title to head of rugby culture and wine consultant after failing to follow media commitments at the league's season launch and opening match.

Sarries new chief executive Ed Coetzee on Friday ended the confusion on Friday by confirming Venter as head of culture and technical director, a role which will include "significant media duties".

Venter duly spoke to TNT Sports before the clash with Sale and said he refused the director's title because he had "absolutely nothing" to do with other sections of the club such as the academy and women's section.

The 56-year-old also insisted the wine consultant reference was not a joke aimed at the media.

"Our whole theme this year was all about wine," Venter told TNT Sports. "Everything in our theme was about a blend and getting the blend right.

"There's nobody in life that is successful by doing one thing the whole time, it doesn't work like that. As you grow older you have to blend things so that's where it came from, and it's very relevant."

Chris Jones, BBC Rugby Union correspondent

The Prem has been all about free flowing attack so far this season, but this was much more of an old school dogfight.

A stop-start game dominated by the referee's whistle, Sale came up with two big plays in the second half: Tom O'Flaherty with a stunning individual score, while Ben Bamber's try was also a beauty after excellent build-up play.

The big names stepped up for Sale. Courtney Lawes looked his old self in the lineout and on the floor, while Tom Curry was magnificent in the kind of physical scrap he relishes. George Ford managed the game beautifully in the closing stages.

Sarries director of rugby turned wine consultant turned technical director Brendan Venter again handed media duties over to head coach Joe Shaw post-match, but he will talk this week in a bid to avoid further sanctions from Prem Rugby.

'Jibulu could explode onto international scene' - reaction

"We couldn't really get into our flow, that's the truth of it. Credit to Sale, they came and fronted up.

"They had adversity, which we had last weekend, but they kept coming. We have to take it on the chin and move on."

"Any time you watch Nathan (Jibulu) play he makes an impact.

"He was a wrecking ball and caused havoc around the field. He nailed his line-outs and showed he's of international class.

"You can get away with being fast and skilful in the Prem, but it's another level again in terms of the power that's required at international level and he's got that ability. He's immensely strong.

"This could be the season when he explodes onto the international scene."

Saracens: Daly; J Bracken, Tompkins, Va'enuku, Segun; Burke, Williams; Mawi, Dan, Street, Itoje (c), Tizard, Isiekwe, Gonzalez, Barbeary.

Replacements: Clarke, O'Driscoll, Clarey, Martin, Michelow, Earl, C Bracken, Malins.

Replacements: Caine, McIntyre, Francis, Tshiunza, Canakaivata, Hanson, Louw, Loganimasi.

articles.title: Gallagher Prem: Sale Sharks defy Jacques Vermeulen's first-half red card to beat Saracens
articles.summary: Sale Sharks' Jacques Vermeulen received a 20-minute red card for a tackle on Tomos Williams in the first half; Sale's Alex Lozowski had also seen yellow for a similar offence; Sale managed to hold on and get the win
articles.body:
Vermeulen was shown a 20-minute red for a dangerous tackle on Tomos Williams at a point in the first half when Alex Lozowski was in the sin bin because of the same offence.

Saracens then took control but it was only temporary and in the 41st minute O'Flaherty produced the match's pivotal moment by racing over for a dynamic solo try.

It was part of a dominant second half from Sale, who capitalised on the hosts' lifeless performance to bounce back after losing to Bristol on the opening weekend with their hooker Nathan Jibulu also outstanding.

Referee Joe James and TMO Hamish Smales experienced a busy opening half an hour, issuing two cards and disallowing a Saracens try.

It had started so well for Sale when Jibulu finished a driving maul but soon after centre Lozowski was sent to the sin bin for a high tackle on Alfie Barbeary, who was forced off for an HIA.

Worse was to come when Vermeulen was given his marching orders for a dangerous challenge on Williams as the Sharks looked to press home an attack down the right touchline.

It meant Saracens were given the opportunity to play against 13 for three minutes and Sale's situation would have deteriorated further had Courtney Lawes not seen an attempted deliberate knock go backwards.

Almost immediately the hosts appeared to have taken advantage but a Nick Tompkins try was ruled out because of obstruction by Nick Isiekwe and it was not until Eroni Mawi bundled over in the 34th minute that they were off the mark.

For all Saracens' sustained pressure they still trailed 7-5 and a minute into the second half that became 14-5 after O'Flaherty caught a George Ford up and under that went sideways and then slipped through the home defence before sprinting over.

Sale ran out of tacklers to enable Sione Va'enuku to strike back almost immediately but they resumed on the front foot and were frustrated to be penalised just short of the whitewash on two occasions.

They continued knocking on the door and suddenly changed pace with a series of runs gaining yards until Ford sent Ben Bamber galloping over.

Sale now led 21-10 and Saracens' dismal afternoon continued when Theo Dan limped off while his fellow hooker Jamie George watched from the stands, sidelined by injury.

Charlie Bracken combined with brother Jack to race over with eight minutes to go and the Sharks then let another commanding position slip away because of a penalty close to the line, but they had already done enough to see off Saracens.

articles.title: Rugby fans descend on Wakefield for celebratory bus parade
articles.summary: The city has been alive with celebrations after Trinity brought home the Super League trophy.
articles.body:
Thousands of rugby league fans turned out to watch an open-top bus parade, after Wakefield Trinity were crowned Super League champions.

Trinity beat Warrington Wolves 23-10 in Saturday's Grand Final at Old Trafford - their first title win since 1968, long before Super League was established.

To celebrate the victory, two buses, carrying players and staff, travelled from the club's ground at Belle Vue to Wakefield Town Hall for a civic reception.

Fullback Max Jowitt, who has made 188 appearances for Trinity and scored three goals in the final, said the parade had been an "unbelievable" experience.

"The fans have been unbelievable, the city is unbelievable and the trophy's unbelievable," he said.

Fans lined city centre streets to see the buses, which arrived at Wakefield Town Hall at about 15:00.

Jane Robinson became a Wakefield Trinity fan through her late husband, who supported the side from childhood.

She was at the game at Old Trafford, where the team became only the sixth club to win the Super League title.

"It was absolutely out of this world - the atmosphere was electric," she said.

"You can't help but think how good this has been for Wakefield."

Also revelling in the excitement from being at the game, young fan Jasper was wearing a tri-coloured wig his grandfather bought him.

He said "everyone was screaming and shouting" each time Trinity scored a try.

"It's amazing - it's an incredible feeling," added his mum Sarah.

Claire Slater, who was watching alongside her son Cohen, said she felt "absolutely ecstatic".

"The atmosphere yesterday at the ground was absolutely electric, so we wanted to come for the atmosphere today. It's been years in the making hasn't it?"

Melvyn Moyes, who was in the city centre with his brother Ken to cheer on the team, described the atmosphere as "buzzing".

"I can remember the good old days – and the bad old days," Melvyn said.

"Wakefield is back – look out everybody."

Following the reception, a free ticketed fan celebration was held at WX on Union Street with player appearances, speeches and highlights from the Grand Final on big screens.

articles.title: England Rugby League World Cup squad: Jake Connor out, Mikey Lewis in
articles.summary: Leeds Rhinos half-back Jake Connor is left out of England's Rugby League World Cup squad, with Hull KR's Mikey Lewis beating him to a place.
articles.body:
Jake Connor missed out on a Rugby League World Cup spot by a "small margin" as England seek the players who can best stick to their gameplan, head coach Brian McDermott says.

Leeds Rhinos half-back Connor, the 2025 Super League Man of Steel, was left out of the 23-man squad for the tournament - to be held largely in Australia - with Hull KR's Mikey Lewis making the cut instead.

For Connor, it is another England disappointment to follow his controversial omission from the squad for last autumn's home series against Australia.

"Jake Connor missed out on selection by a small margin and it came down to who I think can best stick to the game plan and attack plan," McDermott said.

The 31-year-old had been expected to make the squad after being talked up by McDermott and enjoying a strong domestic season.

But Hull KR's Lewis, who endured an inconsistent year, has done enough to convince McDermott that he should join captain George Williams, the Warrington stand-off, and Wigan's Harry Smith as half-back options.

England begin their World Cup campaign against Tonga in Perth on 17 October, before facing France in the same city on 24 October and then Papua New Guinea in Wollongong on 30 October.

England squad: Matty Ashton (Warrington Wolves), AJ Brimson (Gold Coast Titans), Ben Currie (Warrington Wolves), Zach Eckersley (Wigan Warriors), Herbie Farnworth (Dolphins), Ethan Havard (Wigan Warriors), Max King (Bulldogs), Morgan Knowles (Dolphins), Mikey Lewis (Hull KR), Jez Litten (Hull KR), Junior Nsemba (Wigan Warriors), Brad O'Neill (Wigan Warriors), Kai Pearce-Paul (Wests Tigers), Victor Radley (Sydney Roosters), Hugo Savala (Sydney Roosters), Harry Smith (Wigan Warriors), Morgan Smithies (Canberra Raiders), Luke Thompson (Wigan Warriors), Sam Walters (Wigan Warriors), Ben Talty (Brisbane Broncos), Jack Welsby (St Helens), George Williams (Warrington Wolves), Dom Young (Newcastle Knights)

Australia-born Strange in England World Cup squad

Hawkins among five World Cup winners in England squad

There has been much debate about which half-backs would make the England squad after McDermott said last month that he would probably take three to the World Cup, and that captain Williams - who is heading to Australia to join NRL club Dolphins after the tournament - would be one of them.

McDermott said: "Jake has had a really good year. He had an outstanding year last year and got Man of Steel.

"What I've got is a squad full of players who I believe will best play to the game style, the attack plan or game model we identified many weeks ago, that I think we need to compete with the leading nations.

"We can't do the usual things, and I made this a point when I took the job. We've got to play with a point of difference.

"I've got a squad here who I believe are best suited to the attack plan and game model I think England need to play."

Explaining his decision to select Lewis, McDermott added: "I've picked a group of player that have recent history of playing in finals, winning finals, delivering when it matters.

"Mikey Lewis won a World Club Challenge at the start of this year and guided his team to a Challenge Cup final.

"I get he wasn't in the best of shape towards the back of the year and incurred a couple of bans but again, I'll just point people to the attack plan and game model I think England need to have to compete with the leading nations."

Chance for Savala, Wakefield quartet injured

When he replaced Shaun Wane as head coach, McDermott indicated that he was keen to use heritage players - those who qualify for England through family background - to ensure the strongest possible squad.

He has called up two uncapped Australia-born players - versatile back Hugo Savala, part of Sydney Roosters' NRL Grand Final-winning squad, and Brisbane Broncos' front-rower Ben Talty.

Bulldogs prop Max King, born in Huddersfield while his Australian father David was a player there, also earns a first call-up. Victor Radley and AJ Brimson complete the Australia-born contingent in the squad.

Grand Final winners Wakefield have no players in the squad, with Tom Johnstone, Mike McMeeken, Caleb Hamlin-Uele and Jake Trueman all needing time to recover from injuries.

"It's a real shame that the Wakefield boys aren't available," McDermott said. "There's nothing we or they can do. They're all booked in for operations at the end of the year."

And also injured were Sydney Roosters centre Billy Smith - a scorer in Sunday's NRL Grand Final - Wigan centre Jake Wardle, Leeds winger Ash Handley and prop Mikolaj Oledzki, who is leaving Headingley to join NRL side Perth Bears.

Grand Finalists Warrington have three players in the squad - Matty Ashton and Ben Currie joining captain Williams - while Wigan have seven, including Man of Steel winner Brad O'Neill and uncapped centre Zach Eckersley.

Lewis provides off-the-bench spark - analysis

Mikey Lewis over Jake Connor feels like a call made based on pace rather than any other metric, as the Hull KR half is much more of a runner than his opposite number.

He's also perhaps more of an off-the-bench spark than the Leeds playmaker, given George Williams and Harry Smith's blend of run threat and game management will probably get the nod at six and seven.

Herbie Farnworth has been one of the best players in the world for some time and has taken his game to new levels in 2026, and getting the centre involved must be among Brian McDermott's biggest tactical challenges.

Dom Young is another thoroughbred who England will look to out wide, having helped Newcastle to the NRL Grand Final.

Victor Radley's influence and savage tackling makes him a shoo-in for the pack, something that was missed in last year's Ashes series against Australia, and there are other big hitters in the ranks with Morgan Knowles and Morgan Smithies also sharpened by their NRL exploits, and Brad O'Neill back in the international picture after a Man of Steel year.

Staying with the pack, the prospect of a Kai Pearce-Paul and Junior Nsemba second-row pairing whets the appetite.

Elsewhere, the new imports from the NRL have pedigree; Max King has played State of Origin, Hugo Savala can jump into a number of backs spots and Ben Talty is an athletic front-rower who helped Brisbane to success in 2025.

Zach Eckersley has impressed for Wigan this year, and his strong build and athleticism - coupled with an ability to put a winger away - make him a solid inclusion, while Matty Ashton's return after his missed the Ashes with an anterior cruciate knee ligament injury gives England genuine pace out wide.

Everyone will have their opinion on the squad, which features no selections from Super League champions Wakefield - albeit with some contenders unavailable - but there is a balance to the selection.

McDermott has said England might need something different to truly test the best, and it is that conundrum which will again be at the forefront of his thoughts.

Reece Walsh has secured a place in Australia's men's World Cup squad, also named on Monday - although head coach Kevin Walters has refused to confirm whether he will be first-choice full-back.

Walsh has struggled to hit the heights of last season, when he inspired Brisbane Broncos to their first NRL Grand Final triumph in 19 years before helping Australia to a 3-0 Test series win over England.

He missed the end of this season to have ankle surgery, but with Penrith's Dylan Edwards ruled out of the World Cup with a knee injury, Walsh will vie for the full-back spot with James Tedesco - man of the match as Sydney Roosters beat Newcastle Knights 19-18 in Sunday's NRL Grand Final.

Loose forward Isaah Yeo will delay surgery on a torn pectoral muscle to captain Australia.

Winger Mark Nawaqanitawase - who scored two tries in Sydney's win on Sunday - is not in the squad because of his impending code switch to union with Japanese side Saitama Wild Knights. Second-row forward Angus Crichton is absent for the same reason, as he is joining NSW Waratahs.

Star half-back Nathan Cleary is out of the tournament with a broken ankle.

Dual-code winger Nawaqanitawase stars as Roosters win NRL Final

Ali Brigginshaw has missed out on the chance to go for a fourth World Cup winners' medal after being omitted from Australia's women's squad.

Head coach Jess Skinner said the 36-year-old Brisbane half-back - Australia's captain when they won the tournament in Manchester four years ago - was "upset" to be left out.

"That was one of the hardest phone calls I've had to make as a coach to a player and to talk about her and where she was," Skinner said.

articles.title: Rugby League World Cup 2026: England name 23-player squad as Jake Connor misses out and Mikey Lewis earns call-up
articles.summary: Hull KR's Mikey Lewis has been named ahead of Leeds Rhinos' Jake Connor in Brian McDermott's 23-man England squad for the 2026 Rugby League World Cup; Wakefield's Caleb Hamlin-Uele misses out due to injury
articles.body:
Connor, who won last year's Super League Man of Steel award, is the surprise omission, having enjoyed another standout season with the Rhinos, amassing 43 assists - the most of any player this season.

Hull KR playmaker Lewis will come into the fold in his place, having scored 17 tries and assisting a further 14 this season.

It is also understood Wakefield Trinity prop Caleb Hamlin-Uele and his team-mate Tom Johnstone both opted to withdraw from the selection process due to injury. Jake Trueman was another player omitted due to injury.

England commence their Rugby League World Cup campaign against Tonga on Saturday, October 17, at HBF Park, Perth, Australia, before facing France on October 24.

McDermott has named seven Wigan Warriors players in his squad, including uncapped centre Zach Ecersley, Harry Smith and Junior Nsemba.

After winning Sunday's NRL Grand Final, Sydney Roosters lock Victor Radley will return to the England fold, while his Roosters team-mate Hugo Savala has also been selected.

Savala is one of five uncapped players included in the squad, including Eckersley, Brisbane Broncos duo Max King and Ben Talty, and Sam Walters.

Dally M centre of the year Herbie Farnworth and NRL Grand Finalist Dom Young, two of England's top performers at the 2022 World Cup, will also return to the side.

A quartet of other NRL players will join them, including Gold Coast Titans fullback AJ Brimson, West Tigers' Kai Pearce-Paul and Morgan Smithies of the Canberra Raiders.

Fresh from guiding Warrington Wolves to the Super League Grand Final, George Williams will once again captain the team. He is joined in the squad by Wolves team-mates Ashton and Currie.

Jez Litten will join his Hull KR team-mate Lewis in the squad, while Jack Welsby is St Helens' lone representative.

"We have selected the squad after a thorough and deliberate process, underpinned by a unique decentralised preparation model that has allowed us to work closely with the players well before they come together in camp," McDermott said.

"Throughout that process, we have challenged players to develop a deeper understanding of themselves - their strengths, their point of difference, the areas they need to improve and the standards required to perform at international level.

"Importantly, we have also developed a much deeper understanding of the expectations around each player's specific role within the England Game Model.

"The aim has been that when the players arrive in camp, they are not starting from day one trying to understand what is expected of them. They already understand their role, the standards attached to it and how their individual strengths can contribute to the way England wants to play."

articles.title: England's Rugby League World Cup squad: Brian McDermott explains Jake Connor exclusion, Mikey Lewis inclusion, and game plan
articles.summary: England head coach Brian McDermott has named his 23-player squad for the upcoming Rugby League World Cup; He has chosen to leave Jake Connor out, citing big game experience and the 'game model' that England want to play with
articles.body:
Connor was controversially left out of England's 3-0 Ashes drubbing last autumn by then head coach Shaun Wane and has once again had a strong season for Leeds Rhinos that led to his Dream Team inclusion.

However, McDermott has opted for George Williams, Harry Smith, and Mikey Lewis as his half-back options, with Sydney Roosters centre Hugo Savala also a capable half-back.

For McDermott, the players in that heavy Ashes defeat series were not the issue, but the game plan enforced that has been tried and failed many times before.

"It is not a case of changing players as such, although through the tournament we will pick the team that we think can best get the job done each week, but I believe last year that they didn't play with the points of difference," McDermott said.

"They just tried the usual things - they tried to put the ball on a certain pat of grass and then tried to shift the ball to beat Australia on the outside.

"I don't suggest that's what England's done all the time but you have got to play with the point of difference and the reason not many people will do it is because sometimes it doesn't come off and there's a risk element to that.

"You have got to have some courage. There is a way of playing which asks more questions of team's defence when you have got the ball rather than just loading up for one shape per set."

Lewis has done it in 'big games' and 'runs' the ball

While McDermott believes Lewis fits the "game model" more than Connor, he understands that, on form, Connor has had a strong season.

However, alongside form, having led a team in a big game also came into his thinking, which he noted Lewis did in the Challenge Cup and World Club Challenge.

"I believe Jake's had a really good year. He had an outstanding year last year, got a Man of Steel and again has played with a leading team this year," he added.

"What I have got is a squad full of players who I believe will best play to the game style, the attack plan or the game model that we identified many weeks ago that I think we need to do to be able to compete with the leading nations.

"We can't do the usual things and I've made this a point from the day that I took the job, we've got to play with the point of difference.

"So I've got a squad of players here that I believe are best suited to the attack plan and the game model that I think England need to play.

"I think form, current form has a bearing, of course it does. I think there's another principle of how we've picked a team as well which is can you play under pressure.

"The World Cup and internationally you don't get any second chances, you have to deliver there and then, you cannot go back and review the game and have another go the following week.

"I have picked a group of players who've got recent history of playing in finals, winning finals, delivering when it matters.

"Mikey Lewis won a World Cup Challenge at the start of this year and guided his team to a Challenge Cup final.

"I get that he wasn't in the best of shape towards the back end of the year and incurred a couple of bans there, but again, I will just point everybody to the attack plan and the game model that I think that England needs to have to be able to compete with the nations."

With big game experience identified, there was another word that McDermott also focused on when discussing his decision to go with Lewis over Connor: "Well the guy runs and when he is in doubt he runs," McDermott said.

"He doesn't die wondering Mikey, he brings a lot of energy, he brings a lot of attitude and at times that spills over and that would be a concern for any coach.

"But the game is played over the gain line and international football, everything is over the gain line.

"If you look at the Grand Final last night in Australia, there weren't too many tries where people shifted the ball from left side to the right side of the field- everything is nice and tight and everything is over the gain line.

"So you have got some players that, when everybody else is tired, they'll carry the ball themselves and Mikey Lewis does that tremendously well."

It is noticeable that Super League Grand Final winners Wakefield Trinity do not have any inclusions in the England squad - they have Jake Trueman, Mike McMeeken, Caleb Hamlin-Uele, and Tom Johnstone in the extended squad.

However, McDermott revealed all four of those players withdrew through injury as recently as the morning of the announcement.

"It is a real shame that the Wakefield boys aren't available. There's nothing we could do or they could do," McDermott said.

"They are all booked in for operations at the end of the year. Jake Truman in particular has had a fantastic year. Mike McMeeken has been enormous. He's been enormous through finals. Same with Caleb Hamlin-Uele and Tom Johnstone.

"So every single one of them were in amongst being picked, but I knew they were going to have operations and there's a strong likelihood that some of them might not be available and I just got a message."

articles.title: Prem talking points: Louis Rees-Zammit's celebration and England bolters
articles.summary: Bristol set out their top-four aspirations with a statement win, while Gloucester's renaissance continues in the second round of Prem action.
articles.body:
The stats piled up after a car-crash performance by Harlequins in a 48-0 shellacking by Gloucester.

The biggest league defeat in 26 years. Seventeen penalties conceded. Only two entries made into the opposition 22m. Not one of their starting forward pack making more than four carries.

It was a desperately under-powered display.

Boss Jason Gilmore described it as "totally unacceptable" in the aftermath.

The Australian has overseen a few eyesores during his time in charge; a 38-0 reverse at Sandy Park and a 40-14 reverse at the club's festive fixture at Allianz Stadium come to mind.

Gilmore says turning around the tanker will take time. Contracts have to run down and money reassigned to different areas of the squad.

Full-back George Furbank was this summer's big investment. The 29-year-old marked his Prem debut for his new club with a couple of trademark breaks, slicing up from backfield.

He is a classy addition, but is he the signing they needed, with little room to manoeuvre under the salary cap and a creaking forward pack limiting the supply of ball to the backline?

England loosehead prop Fin Baxter has been out for 10 months with a foot injury, but should be back soon. South African tighthead Sampie Swiegers is in contention for selection after his arrival in London.

Chandler Cunningham-South and Guido Petti may be due a run from the start.

But, with Alex Dombrandt expected to miss the majority of the season with a knee ligament injury sustained in June, Quins will need them all to hit the ground running.

Snarl up front, rather than style out back, is where they are lacking.

Gloucester thrash sorry Quins to go top of the Prem

Bristol chief executive Tom Tainton caught some flak earlier this year for saying the Bears needs to think like a marketing agency, rather than a traditional rugby club, , external to grow its fanbase.

The image of Louis Rees-Zammit mimicking Northampton star Henry Pollock's 'pulse-check' celebration, and the delight it sparked among fans, were evidence in his favour however.

A 20,756-strong crowd at Ashton Gate – up 5,000 on their win in the same fixture last year, partly helped by football's international break – relished a spiky performance all round from Rees-Zammit.

The Wales international could easily have had a hat-trick in a 34-26 win over Saints, but was body-checked by Tommy Freeman in pursuit of a final-play chip ahead, earning a penalty try and sending his opposite number on his way with a few blunt observations.

Rees-Zammit, restored to the wing after dabbling at full-back on his return from American football, has four tries already this season and Bristol, who were well in last year's play-off hunt before a dip in form after the Six Nations, are looking ominous.

The next four rounds of action – Saracens (a), Exeter (h), Leicester (h) and Bath (a) – are a big chance to dent some other top-four hopefuls.

Rees-Zammit was not the only wing on a wind-up this weekend either, by the way. Adam Radwan's gleeful celebration of his try for Leicester against former club Newcastle, marking his territory by pointing to the pitch below his studs, drew jeers from the Kingston Park crowd.

Rees-Zammit stars as Bristol power past Northampton

Obano and Stuart stake claim for England's 'bomb squad'

England boss Steve Borthwick was at The Rec on Friday night.

He will have taken particular interest in one 28th-minute scrum.

Beno Obano and Will Stuart, either side of hooker Tom Dunn, made the Exeter front row look as though they were wearing skis rather than studs, sending the visitors skidding backwards at a rate of knots.

Considering Baxter's lack of game time and Bevan Rodd being ruled out of the autumn after wrist surgery, Obano may well be the back-up loosehead option to Ellis Genge for England's Nations Championship campaign.

Stuart's welcome return from an Achilles injury is likely to have him installed as the tighthead replacement behind the excellent Joe Heyes.

Borthwick may well lean into their Bath connection as he rebuilds a 'bomb squad' bench which was crucial to England's good form in 2025.

Gloucester fly-half Charlie Atkinson may well be twisting Borthwick's arm as well.

The 25-year-old has been central to the Cherry and Whites' electric start to the season.

He set up the opening try of their thrashing of Harlequins with a cute jink past Will Porter and then a pinpoint crossfield bomb for Ben Loader a couple of passages later. A hint of a dummy and a dart took Atkinson himself over for his team's fourth.

His substandard goal-kicking may count against him. Of players with a minimum of 10 kicks at goal, only Bath's Santi Carreras had a lower success-rate off the tee in 2025-26. Team-mate George Barton had kicking duties on Saturday.

But if Borthwick wants a back-up stand-off that more closely replicates the playing style of first-choice Fin Smith, Atkinson may be due promotion after three appearances for England A last season.

Bath gain revenge on Exeter to win 11-try thriller

Last year's runners-up Exeter have begun the season with successive defeats, but there was significant improvement on their opening-day defeat by Gloucester as they threatened to climb off the canvas and overturn Bath, just as they did in June's semi-final at The Rec.

A fit, firing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso - 133m carried, nine defenders beaten and two tries - was an obvious plus for the Chiefs.

But Kane James made a major step forward.

The 21-year-old Welsh international, who only made his first Prem start at the beginning of this season, was fearless at the Rec, flying into contact with relish.

As well as that wince-inducing ball-carrying, he was cleaning up on the floor, winning three turnovers.

Australia international Tom Hooper is now back in the south west, but has had a high workload switching between Chiefs and Wallabies' duties.

James has made a decent claim to holding on to his back-row spot a little longer.

With the clock in the red and five points down on the scoreboard, Newcastle Red Bulls smuggled the ball out wide to a full-flight Christian Wade.

The 35-year-old had a corridor of space to accelerate into and 45m to cover to the tryline.

Leicester replacement Tom Whiteley just about managed to shut the gap and, a few phases later, Newcastle infringed to give away a penalty and snuff out any hope of victory.

Like Wade's try record however, it is coming for Newcastle.

After a decent showing in defeat away to champions Northampton in the opening round, Newcastle had the upper hand on Leicester for large stretches.

The visitors made more than double the number of tackles of their opponents.

The accuracy to turn possession into points is one of a number of things that will surely improve steeply as the Newcastle squad, revamped with more than 20 summer signings, gel together.

articles.title: WXV: Nel Metcalfe back in Wales reckoning for double-header Japan Tests
articles.summary: Nel Metcalfe is in a 30-strong party that will be led by co-captains Alex Callender and Kate Williams for back-to-back Tests in Japan.
articles.body:
Full-back Nel Metcalfe has a chance to resurrect her Wales career after being named in Sean Lynn's squad for their WXV double-header against Japan.

The 21-year-old Gloucester-Hartpury player has fully recovered from the knee injury that ruled her out of the 2026 Women's Six Nations.

Lynn named Metcalfe in his extended training squad for the stunning WXV win against South Africa and subsequent defeat by the United States, but she did not make the matchday squads.

Uncapped props Stella Orrin and Crystal James also make the cut in a 30-strong party that will be led by flankers and co-captains Alex Callender and Kate Williams.

But Jaz and Alisha Joyce have not made the squad while wing Seren Singleton, who played her part as Wales beat South Africa, is also omitted.

Lynn remaining positive despite Wales' USA setback

'Lions Women can learn from darts and 1997'

Metcalfe's recovery included facing Barbarians for Wales in June in an uncapped encounter.

After making their debuts in September, wing Amy Williams, prop Elan Jones and hooker Shanelle Williams will also travel to Japan.

Wales will face the hosts at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium, Tokyo on Saturday, 24 October (10:30 BST) followed by their second meeting at Kumagaya Rugby Stadium, Saitama Prefecture seven days later (07:00 GMT).

Lynn said: "This was a tough selection process after our performances against South Africa and USA, we asked the players to move the dial, and we did that in those two Test matches.

"We scored eight tries against South Africa and the disappointment of the players with the two-point deficit against USA, a team ranked sixth in the world, demonstrated the shift in mindset we need.

"All the hard work the players, coaches and staff put in across pre-season was there for all to see and we laid some real foundations in how we want to play and the team's identity.

"We know we have a long way to go before we become the team, we want to be but the tour to play the Sakura XV in Japan is an exciting challenge for us all."

articles.title: Rugby Union Weekly: Danny Care says Saracens bosses have "let players down"
articles.summary: Former England scrum-half Danny Care says "some of the powers that be" at Saracens have "let the players down".
articles.body:
Former England scrum-half Danny Care says "some of the powers that be" at Saracens have "let the players down" after a turbulent start to the season.

An opening weekend 40-38 win at Leicester was followed by a 21-17 home defeat by Sale , the build-up to which was marred by headlines made by returning director of rugby Brendan Venter.

He reportedly refused to perform a series of media obligations , putting Saracens at risk of fines amid conjecture his job title had been changed to 'head of rugby culture and wine consultant', although the club have since clarified he is now head of culture and technical director.

"They're putting the players under more pressure with off-field antics", Care told the BBC's Rugby Union Weekly podcast.

"The lads don't want a part of any of that, they just want to play.

"There was all this chat of Sarries pushing for top four again, and having this amazing team and culture again.

"I just think some of the powers that be at the top have let the players down."

New Saracens chief executive Ed Coetzee confirmed on Friday that Venter's job title, which differs to the one he was said to have when appointed to succeed Mark McCall, includes "significant media duties".

Venter duly spoke to TNT Sports before the match with Sale and said he refused the director of rugby job title because he had "absolutely nothing" to do with other departments of the club, such as the academy and women's section.

The 56-year-old also insisted the wine consultant reference was not a joke aimed at the media.

"Our whole theme this year was all about wine," Venter said. "Everything in our theme was about a blend and getting the blend right."

But Care said the stories around Venter's role looked to have had a negative impact on the pitch.

"Sarries have done some amazing things in the last year or so, bringing a new energy, a new vibe," he said.

"But then it just feels like they're taking the mickey out of everyone by [saying] 'he's not doing interviews today' and taking fines and changing his job title.

"You can only do that when you are so much better at rugby than everyone else and at the moment, they're not.

"[The performance against Sale] looked flat. It looked quiet. I don't blame the players. I blame the management for that."

articles.title: Red Roses: England's Marlie Packer to miss WXV Global Series matches against Canada and USA in North America
articles.summary: England play Canada in Toronto and Ottawa on October 17 and 24 respectively before game versus USA in New Jersey a week later; back-rower Marlie Packer staying at home with partner Rosie Galligan due to give birth; Canada ended England's 39-match winning run in September with 26-26 draw
articles.body:
Two-time World Cup winner Packer, who has made 119 appearances for her country, will remain at home with partner and Red Roses team-mate Rosie Galligan due to give birth.

England play Canada in Toronto and Ottawa on October 17 and 24 respectively before a game versus USA in New Jersey on October 30.

Delaney Burns, Haidee Head and Sophie McQueen are ruled out through injury.

The Red Roses played three times in September, beating Australia and New Zealand around a 26-26 draw with Canada in Exeter that ended the hosts' 39-match winning streak.

Head coach John Mitchell said: Our last two Tests against Canada and New Zealand have been humdingers that could have gone either way. They were hugely important to our development towards [the 2029 World Cup].

"Playing quality opposition and learning to adapt under pressure will help us raise our level and improve our game.

"The 32 players travelling to North America have a great opportunity to elevate our connections as a squad because playing away from home requires togetherness.

"We have shown a real hunger to compete and improve, and we're excited to rip into our preparations and continue our rivalry with Canada in Toronto."

articles.title: Ward ruled out of Munster game but trio return
articles.summary: Back row Bryn Ward is ruled out of Ulster's interprovincial United Rugby Championship game against Munster but Jacob Stockdale, Robert Baloucoune and Scott W...
articles.body:
Ulster back row Bryn Ward has been ruled out of Saturday's United Rugby Championship game against Munster because of a knee injury.

Ward sustained the problem in last weekend's dramatic 33-33 draw with Glasgow Warriors at Scotstoun.

Scrum-half Matthew Devine is a doubt for the interprovincial encounter at the Affidea Stadium, which has a 17:30 BST kick-off.

The former Connacht player is carrying a shoulder injury and his fitness for selection will be assessed later this week.

On a more positive note for Ulster head coach Richie Murphy, Jacob Stockdale has returned to full training after overcoming the hip injury which forced him to withdraw from the starting line-up for the meeting with Glasgow.

Similarly, Scott Wilson (ankle) and Robert Baloucoune (concussion) have are both fit for selection after injuries.

Ulster are still aiming to secure their first URC win of the season after an opening weekend defeat by Edinburgh in Belfast was followed by a draw in Glasgow.

Munster beat the Bulls in Limerick on Saturday after losing to Glasgow Warriors at Thomond Park seven days earlier.
